statsmodels.simple: A classic Python library for statistics. Its tsa module has ADF, ACF, STL, Holt-Winters, ARIMA and SARIMAX.

stationary.simple: A series whose average and spread do not change over time.
stationary.example: Daily temperature changes (differences) are often stationary.

ADF test.simple: Augmented Dickey-Fuller test. Its null hypothesis is that the series has a unit root (is not stationary). A small p-value means it looks stationary.

unit root.simple: A feature of a series, such as a random walk, that makes it non-stationary. Differencing removes it.
unit root.example: A random walk has a unit root.

p-value.simple: The probability of seeing a result at least this extreme if the null hypothesis were true. Small means the null is unlikely.
p-value.example: p = 0.01 in the ADF test: reject the unit root.

ACF.simple: Autocorrelation function: the correlation of a series with itself at each lag.
ACF.example: An ACF peak at lag 7 suggests a weekly season.

PACF.simple: Partial autocorrelation function: the correlation at a lag after removing the effect of the shorter lags.
PACF.example: A PACF that cuts off after lag 2 suggests AR(2).

STL.simple: Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess. It splits a series into trend, seasonal and residual parts.

Holt-Winters.simple: Exponential smoothing with a level, a trend and a seasonal part, each updated with its own smoothing weight.

ARIMA.simple: A model with p autoregressive terms, d differences and q moving-average terms: ARIMA(p, d, q).

exogenous variable.simple: An outside input to a model, such as price or holiday flag, not produced by the series itself.

AIC.simple: Akaike information criterion: a score of fit that punishes extra parameters. Lower is better, only for models on the same data.

Ljung-Box test.simple: A test of whether residuals still have autocorrelation. A small p-value means the model misses structure.

long format.simple: A table with one row per series and time point, with columns unique_id, ds and y. Many series are stacked.

statsforecast.simple: A Nixtla library with fast classical models such as AutoETS, AutoARIMA and Theta for many series.

mlforecast.simple: A Nixtla library that builds lag features and trains regressors such as LightGBM for many series.

reconciliation.simple: Adjusting forecasts at several levels so that lower levels add up to higher levels.
reconciliation.example: Store forecasts sum to the national forecast.

TimeGPT.simple: A forecasting foundation model from Nixtla that you call through a web API.

framework.simple: A library that gives one interface for many models, with data handling, backtesting and metrics.

Darts.simple: A Python forecasting library with one API for classical, machine learning and deep models.

sktime.simple: A scikit-learn style Python toolkit for time series forecasting, classification and clustering.

forecasting horizon.simple: The steps ahead you want to forecast.

aeon.simple: A Python toolkit for time series machine learning: classification, clustering, regression and distances.
aeon.example: A fork of sktime with a focus on ML.

AutoML.simple: Software that tries many models and settings for you and combines the best.

tsfresh.simple: A library that extracts many statistical features from each time series and selects useful ones.

DTW.simple: Dynamic time warping: a distance between two series that allows shifts and stretches in time.
DTW.example: Compare two heartbeats of different speed.

matrix profile.simple: For each window of a series, the distance to its nearest similar window. Low values are repeated patterns, high values are unusual ones.

online learning.simple: A model that updates after each new example and does not need the full dataset.

PyOD.simple: A Python library with many outlier detectors under one interface.

prequential evaluation.simple: Test-then-train on a stream: predict each new example first, then learn from it.

backtest.simple: Testing a forecasting method on past data by forecasting from several earlier cutoffs and comparing with what happened.
